rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Electron pairs repel; geometry is the truce. VSEPR counts the domains around the central atom — bonding pairs plus lone pairs, multiple bonds counting once — and spreads them to minimum repulsion: two domains linear (BeCl₂, CO₂), three trigonal planar (BF₃), four tetrahedral (CH₄), five trigonal bipyramidal (PCl₅, axial 219 pm vs equatorial 204 pm), six octahedral (SF₆).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Domains = BP + LP (multiple bond = 1 domain) - Angle compression: each LP ≈ −2 to −2.5° (second-row centres) - Repulsion: lp–lp > lp–bp > bp–bp

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Domains, not bonds:** double bonds are one domain each — counting CO₂ as four domains gives a false tetrahedral answer.  ·  **Lone pairs shape the molecule but never name it:** "pyramidal" and "bent" describe atom positions; the lone pair is the invisible puppeteer.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Specialized insight for 06 vsepr theory and shapes of simple molecules.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***PCl₅'s two bond lengths*** — axial 219 pm vs equatorial 204 pm: the axial pair suffers 90° repulsion from three neighbours, the equatorial only two — VSEPR's repulsion logic made measurable.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Domain count → geometry: "2 lin, 3 tri, 4 tet, 5 TBP, 6 oct." Angle ladder: CH₄ 109.5 > NH₃ 107 > H₂O 104.5 > H₂S 92 > PH₃ 93 (≈). Lone pairs: subtract 2–2.5° each (2nd row).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2022 (3m): Predict the shape, hybridisation and bond angle of (a) PCl₅ (b) SF₆ (c) BeCl₂ (d) H₂S using VSEPR theory.** — **(a) PCl₅:** five bond pairs, no lone pair → **trigonal bipyramidal** (sp³d); three equatorial P–Cl at 120°, two axial at 90°; axial bonds longer (219 pm) than equatorial (204 pm).…  ·  **NEB 2020 (3m): Using VSEPR theory, explain the shape of ammonia, its hybridisation and bond angle. Why is its bond angle less than that of methane?** — Nitrogen in NH₃ carries three bond pairs and **one lone pair** — four electron domains with tetrahedral electron geometry (sp³ hybridisation).…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Every shape answer: domain count → electron geometry → lone-pair correction → shape name + angle. Four lines, full marks. For PCl₅ add the axial/equatorial distinction — it is the mark-separator.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: One count — bonding pairs + lone pairs — drives everything: the domain number fixes the electron geometry; the lone-pair number fixes the distortion and the shape name. NH₃ vs CH₄ (NEB 2024) and H₂O vs CO₂ (NEB 2024) are the two contrasts to rehearse.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: VSEPR postulates: shape set by central-atom electron pairs; minimum repulsion = maximum separation; lp–lp > lp–bp > bp–bp; multiple bond = one domain. Parent geometries: 2 linear 180°, 3 trigonal planar 120°, 4 tetrahedral 109.5°, 5 TBP 120/90, 6 octahedral 90.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Water's 104.5° angle is why ice's open lattice floats — the bent shape propagates from VSEPR to climate.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (3m): Explain why H₂O is bent while CO₂ is linear.** — **CO₂:** carbon has two electron domains (two C=O double bonds — each counts once) and **no lone pairs**; minimum repulsion puts the domains 180° apart → **linear**.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Geometry from Repulsion Electron pairs are all negatively charged — they repel. **VSEPR** (valence shell electron pair repulsion) turns that single fact into molecular architecture: the pairs around a central atom spread as far apart as possible, and the geometry they form is the molecule's shape.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Postulates 1. The shape of a molecule is set by the **total number of electron pairs** in the valence shell of the central atom. 2. The pairs **repel one another** and adopt the arrangement of **minimum repulsion / maximum separation**. 3.…  ·  ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Value to quote | |---|---|---| | **VSEPR theory** | Shape predicted by minimising repulsion of electron pairs around the central atom | Gillespie–Nyholm | | **Electron geometry** | Arrangement of all domains (bonds + lone pairs) | NH₃: tetrahedral | | **Molecular shape** | Arrangement of atoms only | NH₃: pyramidal | |…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6. Common Confusions **Electron geometry ≠ molecular shape:** NH₃'s electron geometry is tetrahedral but its shape is pyramidal — the shape name counts atoms only.  ·  **Multiple bonds count once:** CO₂ has two domains (not four) — each double bond is one region of electron density.  ·  **H₂S is not "mini-water":** same domain count, but 92° vs 104.5° — larger, more diffuse lone pairs on sulphur and longer S–H bonds change the balance; never copy water's angle.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 7. Exam Application **Verified PYQ (NEB 2022): Predict the shape, hybridisation and bond angle of (a) PCl₅ (b) SF₆ (c) BeCl₂ (d) H₂S.** — (a) PCl₅: 5 BP → trigonal bipyramidal, sp³d, 120°/90°. (b) SF₆: 6 BP → octahedral, sp³d², 90°. (c) BeCl₂: 2 BP → linear, sp, 180°.…  ·  **Verified PYQ (NEB 2024/04): Predict the shapes of BF₃ and PCl₅ using VSEPR theory. Give their hybridisation.** — BF₃: three bond pairs, no lone pair → trigonal planar, 120°, sp². PCl₅: five bond pairs → trigonal bipyramidal (3 equatorial at 120°, 2 axial at 90°), sp³d.  ·  **Verified PYQ (NEB 2024/02): Why is NH₃ pyramidal while CH₄ is tetrahedral, though both have four electron pairs?** — Both have tetrahedral electron geometry. In CH₄ all four pairs are bond pairs and all four corners carry H atoms → tetrahedral, 109.5°.…
